stem: Two containers use the same substrate recipe, but the shallower container stays wetter for longer after irrigation. Which explanation is best supported by root-zone media principles?
choices: Container geometry can change perched-water behavior even when the substrate recipe is unchanged
The substrate recipe guarantees identical drainage in containers of every shape
Only cultivar identity can explain the difference in dryback
Adding any amendment changes only nutrient concentration and never pore structure
rationale: Container height and geometry affect the proportion and distribution of perched water, so the same medium can drain and dry differently in different containers.
